name: Marcus Atilius Regulus Calenus
summary:
Marcus Atilius Regulus Calenus was a Roman politician and general who played a key role in the Third Punic War. He was born into a wealthy family and received a traditional education, but his actual military career began when he joined the army of Rome at the age of 15. Despite being wounded multiple times, Regulus returned to Rome and eventually became one of the most prominent Roman generals.

Regulus' leadership during the war was marked by several significant events, including his siege of Syracuse and his eventual defeat in Africa. However, his actions had a lasting impact on Roman history, as he helped secure Rome's dominance over Carthage and paved the way for future conquests.

Despite his many accomplishments, Regulus' life was cut short when he died in 260 BCE at the age of approximately 40. His legacy lived on, however, and he remains one of the most famous Roman generals in history.
